description: Failure classification patterns for the cost-aware model retry cascade. A stage failure is only retried with a more capable model when its captured output matches a 'retryable' pattern AND does not match a 'non_retryable' pattern. Non-retryable patterns are checked first and win ties — retrying a bigger model cannot fix a missing file, a permission error, or a failing user-code assertion, so those fail fast to avoid burning budget for an identical result.

non_retryable.pattern: ENOENT|No such file or directory|Cannot find module|MODULE_NOT_FOUND|command not found
non_retryable.reason: Missing file or module — a larger model re-runs into the same missing dependency.
Permission/authorization error — model capability is irrelevant.
Failing tests/assertions reflect user-code behavior, not model incapacity; the build loop owns re-fixing these, not the cascade.
Deterministic syntax/compile error — reproducible regardless of model.
Environment/configuration problem — escalate, do not cascade.

retryable.reason: Transient provider throttling — a retry (possibly on a different model tier) can succeed.

retryable.pattern: timeout|timed out|ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|socket hang up|502|503|504|Internal Server Error|connection reset
retryable.reason: Transient network/API error — retry is warranted.

retryable.pattern: max_tokens|response truncated|incomplete output|output too long|context length exceeded
retryable.reason: Output truncation or context overflow — a more capable model with a larger budget may complete the task.

retryable.pattern: did not produce|empty (response|output)|no changes generated|failed to generate
retryable.reason: Under-capable output — escalating to a stronger model is exactly the cascade's purpose.
